original_groups.text: **Objective.** Determine whether cross-modal attention improves donor-held-out Down syndrome classification over matched token concatenation on paired single-cell RNA and ATAC from thirty developmental-cortex donors [@lattke2026down].

Paired single-cell RNA and ATAC profiles invite fusion models, including cross-modal attention. It remains unclear when attention improves donor-level prediction over simpler fusion that sees the same cells and features. We treat the question as an internal comparison: planted-signal regimes where the joint label is known, and a real donor disease-label task on one developmental-cortex atlas [@lattke2026down]. Donor hold-out follows biological-replicate reasoning in differential expression [@squair2021confronting]; it does not guarantee transportability. We report where the evidence does not support an attention advantage and where controls fail their fixed gates.

Multimodal transformers and attention bottlenecks motivate cross-modal fusion [@tsai2019multimodal; @nagrani2021attention; @vaswani2017attention]; attention-based multiple-instance learning motivates donor bags [@ilse2018attention]. Attention weights are treated as diagnostics to probe, not as explanations [@jain2019attention; @wiegreffe2019attention]. Domain-adversarial training and contrastive pairing objectives appear in the ladder as declared components [@ganin2015unsupervised; @ganin2016domain; @oord2018representation; @radford2021learning]. Gene-activity summaries follow established window practice [@stuart2021signac]; NMF tokens are a classical alternative [@lee1999learning].

Paired single-cell RNA and ATAC profiles invite fusion models, including cross-modal attention. It remains unclear when attention improves donor-level prediction over simpler fusion that sees the same cells and features. We treat the question as an internal comparison: planted-signal regimes where the joint label is known, and a real donor disease-label task on one developmental-cortex atlas [@lattke2026down]. Squair et al. show that differential-expression methods must account for variation between biological replicates [@squair2021confronting]. We choose donor hold-out for this classification comparison; it does not guarantee transportability. We report where the evidence does not support an attention advantage and where controls fail their fixed gates.

Weighted nearest-neighbour integration learns the relative utility of modalities in each cell [@hao2021integrated]. MOFA+ models modalities in a shared sample space [@argelaguet2020mofa]; MultiVI integrates multimodal and single-modality data [@ashuach2023multivi]. Transformers provide attention-based sequence modelling [@vaswani2017attention]; MulT uses pairwise cross-modal attention [@tsai2019multimodal], and attention bottlenecks restrict information exchange between modalities [@nagrani2021attention]. Attention-based multiple-instance learning provides bag-level aggregation [@ilse2018attention]; assigning donors as bags is our adaptation. Jain and Wallace question attention weights as explanations [@jain2019attention], whereas Wiegreffe and Pinter argue that their explanatory value depends on the definition and diagnostic tests [@wiegreffe2019attention]. We probe weights as diagnostics. Our nuisance adversary is motivated by domain-adversarial representation learning [@ganin2015unsupervised; @ganin2016domain]; pairing draws on contrastive predictive coding [@oord2018representation] and image–text matching [@radford2021learning]. Signac estimates activity from gene bodies and upstream regions [@stuart2021signac]; our secondary summary uses gene bodies with flanks at both ends. NMF supplies a non-negative representation [@lee1999learning]; its use for tokens is our adaptation.

lattke2026down.locator: Results: A single-cell gene expression and chromatin accessibility atlas; first paragraph / Fig. 1a–b
lattke2026down.support_paraphrase: Profiling used 10X Multiome in 15 DS and 15 control fetal samples, with 248,998 cells retained after QC. Same-cohort disease groups and paired modality provenance are supported; local sampled counts require the sampling ledger.
lattke2026down.verdict: PASS; methods narrowed to distinguish available cells from sampled analysis

squair2021confronting.support_paraphrase: DE methods ignoring variation between biological replicates are prone to false discoveries. This supports the DE warning; it does not validate donor-held-out classifier performance or mandate our precise bootstrap design.
squair2021confronting.verdict: NARROWED_AND_PASS; both uses distinguish our donor design from published DE findings

hao2021integrated.support_paraphrase: WNN is an unsupervised framework learning each modality’s relative utility in each cell for multimodal integration. The abstract is sufficient for this general claim; no specific RNA–ATAC benchmark or algorithmic reproduction is attributed to it.

argelaguet2020mofa.locator: Abstract; Background paragraph beginning MOFA+, in contrast
argelaguet2020mofa.support_paraphrase: MOFA+ provides scalable multimodal integration and uses a common sample space with measurements from the same cells. No superiority over our neural arms is claimed.

ashuach2023multivi.locator: Abstract; Main paragraphs describing paired and single-modality integration
ashuach2023multivi.support_paraphrase: MultiVI creates joint representations of multiomic data and accommodates missing modalities, integrating multimodal with single-modality datasets.

vaswani2017attention.locator: Abstract; arXiv v7 viewed, first submitted 2017
vaswani2017attention.support_paraphrase: The Transformer uses attention for sequence transduction, without recurrence or convolutions. This is architectural background, not RNA–ATAC or donor-task evidence.

tsai2019multimodal.support_paraphrase: MulT uses directional pairwise cross-modal attention for unaligned multimodal language sequences. Donor bag adaptation is ours, not a reported application.

nagrani2021attention.locator: Abstract, second paragraph; arXiv v3 viewed
nagrani2021attention.support_paraphrase: Multimodal fusion bottlenecks require information exchange through a limited set of latent bottlenecks. Audio-visual results are not transferred to this biological task. The viewed revision notes an AudioSet metric correction; none of those numbers is cited here.

ilse2018attention.support_paraphrase: MIL assigns a class to a bag of instances and uses a permutation-invariant attention aggregation operator. Donor bags are our application; this source does not validate donor biology or explanations for this study.
